content.title: About
content.content: Pork tamale is a traditional Latin American dish consisting of a corn‑based dough filled with seasoned pork, sometimes mixed with vegetables or cheese, wrapped in corn or banana leaves and steamed until tender.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tamales have been prepared for over 5,000 years, originating with the ancient Maya and Aztec civilizations.
More than 100 regional variations exist across Mexico, Central and South America.
They are commonly served during holidays such as Day of the Dead, Christmas, and Independence Day.
Corn husks used for wrapping impart a subtle earthy aroma and keep the tamale moist during cooking.
In some regions banana leaves replace corn husks, giving a distinct flavor and fragrance.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The pork filling provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Tamales contain thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn masa supplies slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Both pork and corn contribute iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The masa and any added vegetables increase fiber content, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn masa.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces or marinades can raise the salt level; adjust added salt accordingly.

items.title: Meat safety
items.content: Improperly cooked pork may harbor pathogens; ensure tamales are steamed until fully done.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Tamales are moderately calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tamales are served hot, unwrapped from their leaf covering. They can be enjoyed plain or topped with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream, often accompanied by beans, rice, and fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked tamales in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in freezer‑safe bags; they retain quality for about 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
